intro_html: Beef bourguignon has a reputation for being fussy French cooking, and it is really just a beef stew with bacon, mushrooms, and a mountain of onions cooked down into the gravy. The cut it calls for is chuck, the same cheap roast in every other braise on this site. The name is expensive, the groceries are not. Each bowl carries 47 grams of protein and 726 calories for about $5.48 (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $5.48 a bowl (at everyday cost) for the dish that gets described as special occasion cooking. Bacon, mushrooms, and onions are doing the work that most people assume the wine does.
shop_smart: This recipe uses onions by the bag, not by the piece. Buy the largest mesh bag your store carries and check the price per pound against the loose bin before you commit.
Mushrooms are the other big produce line. The whole white button mushrooms cost less than the pre sliced trays and take about a minute to slice yourself.
Bacon ends and pieces, where you can get them, are perfect here. Nobody sees the strips once they are chopped into a stew.
Butter goes on sale hard in November and December and freezes for a year. That is the time to buy it for every braise you will make.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in the pot until crisp. Lift it out and leave the fat.
Cut the chuck into large cubes, dry them well, season with salt and black pepper, and brown them hard in the bacon fat and vegetable oil in batches.
Slice the onions and cook them in the same pot, patiently, until they are soft and deeply golden. This takes a while and it is where the sweetness comes from.
Add the garlic, then stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth, scraping the bottom clean, and add the bay leaves and thyme.
Return the beef and bacon, cover, and simmer very low for 2.5 hours, until the beef breaks apart under a spoon.
Saute the sliced mushrooms and the carrots in the butter in a separate pan until browned, then stir them in for the last 20 minutes so they keep their shape.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty-pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Ladle that weight into each of 14 containers, stirring between scoops so the mushrooms and bacon get spread around. Each bowl lands at 726 calories with 47 grams of protein.

steps: Render the bacon until crisp and lift it out, keeping the fat.
Brown the cubed chuck roast in the bacon fat and oil in batches.
Cook the sliced onions until deeply golden, then add garlic, flour, and tomato paste.
Add the beef broth with bay and thyme, return the beef and bacon, and simmer 2.5 hours.
Saute mushrooms and carrots in butter, stir them in at the end, and portion into 14 containers.
